They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Read from the plots, collapse is close to complete on the four easier datasets and partial on ImageNet at the last epoch. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. | [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v4 | In image classifiers, between two networks linearly connected by spawning from a shared checkpoint or by permutation alignment (MLPs, and VGG-16, ResNet-20 and ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet), nearly every layer's features at three points on the line were proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features, and pairs that were not linearly connected were far from it | Zhou et al. | [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) v4 | In a model that decodes the sum of two learned embeddings, at zero training loss with an injective decoder, a training set fixes the generalising representation of addition when its same-answer pairs leave only translation and scale free; for non-modular addition with p = 10 and one-dimensional embeddings, generalisation sets in near the training fraction, about 0.4, at which that becomes likely | Liu et al. (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), in a toy built for it: same-answer training pairs force equal embedding sums, equal sums carry answers to unseen pairs, and for addition with p = 10 the fraction at which the forced equations first pin the embedding to a + kb (about 0.4) matches the onset of generalisation and Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). It is shown for one size, 1D embeddings and an operation built into the architecture. It is not shown that larger networks generalise by this mechanism, and for S₃ the networks generalise beyond it. | Active |
| [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md) v2 | A rank-limited contrastive word embedding trained from small initialisation learns the top eigenvectors of the co-occurrence matrix's relative deviation from independence, one at a time in order of eigenvalue, not the best low-rank approximation of its unconstrained optimum | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md): for the quartic approximation of word2vec with tied weights and symmetric, constant-weight reweighting, the minimisers are proved and the stepwise order is derived, and the prediction matches trained word2vec far better than truncated PMI. | [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md) v2 | When the co-occurrence of words on a latent continuum depends only on their separation, a spectral word embedding places them on the Fourier modes of that continuum, so the circles and rippled curves of months, years and places come from a symmetry of the corpus statistics | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart and Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md): proved for an embedding whose Gram matrix equals the co-occurrence matrix (or its absolute value) at full rank, with the exponential kernel solved for both boundary conditions; the symmetry measured in Wikipedia; matching PCA pictures in Gemma 2. | [THEORY-185](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-185.md) v5 | When each binary attribute of a word affects its co-occurrence independently and multiplicatively, the PMI is affine in the attributes with rank at most d + 1, so a spectral PMI embedding is a linear image of the attribute hypercube and parallelogram analogies hold exactly; over the full hypercube of words, each attribute's two values equally frequent, the raw co-occurrence ratio mixes in products of attributes, and keeps exact analogies only when the strengths are alike enough that every attribute mode outranks every product mode | Korchinski, Karkada, Bahri and Wyart (2025), [LIT-863](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-863.md): proved for a generative model of co-occurrence in which words are bundles of independent binary attributes, with robustness to noise, pruning and deleted pairs argued from eigenvalue bounds and simulated. The embeddings are eigendecompositions, not trained models; that real co-occurrence is close to this form is inferred from spectral and accuracy-curve shapes, not measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) v5 | A deep linear network trained from small weights learns the singular modes of its input–output correlations one at a time in order of strength, each in a sharp sigmoidal transition, while a shallow network learns them all together; the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum, not from nonlinearity | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2019), [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), restating their 2014 solution (LIT-864): exact for decoupled, balanced initial weights and white inputs, simulated for random small weights. With hierarchically generated data the spectrum falls with depth in the tree, so the schedule is coarse to fine. It is not a claim about nonlinear networks, about correlated inputs, or about learning that starts from prior knowledge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md) v2 | Nested angular cones in the Poincaré ball, symmetric about the outward ray with an aperture depending only on the apex's radius, are transitive only if the aperture is at most π/2 and r sin ψ(r)/(1 − r²) does not increase outward; so no such cone can be defined near the origin, the widest admissible family is sin ψ = K(1 − r²)/r, and every point a cone contains lies farther from the origin than its apex | Ganea, Bécigneul and Hofmann (2018), [LIT-866](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-866.md): Lemma 2 and Theorem 3 prove the necessity half under four stated requirements on the cones; the transitivity of the closed-form family (Theorem 4), which the source asserts without proof, is proved in this record's note of 2026-10-19; the radial monotonicity is this record's derivation from the hyperbolic law of cosines. | [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md) v6 | On Monte Carlo samples of the 2D Ising model and of the 2D dimer model with added noise spins, a block coarse-graining trained to maximize mutual information with the system beyond a buffer recovered the variables renormalization already uses (Kadanoff block spins; the dimers' low-momentum electric fields, with no weight on the noise), and iterated on 128 × 128 Ising samples gave the flow away from the critical point, locating it to about 1% and giving ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a restricted Boltzmann machine trained by contrastive divergence on the noisy dimer data coupled to the noise and to columnar patterns instead | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md): shown numerically on two 2D lattice models whose relevant variables were known (Ising block spins, dimer electric fields), with an iterated Ising flow giving T_c to about 1% and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, and analytically only for 1D and quasi-1D chains. | [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) v4 | On the Random Hierarchy Model, in the experiments reported (s = 2, L ≤ 4, small v), deep CNNs matched to the tree and trained in a feature-learning regime reach a tenth of chance error from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, at the training-set size at which their hidden layers become invariant to swapping synonymous tuples; two-layer networks and the same CNNs as fixed kernels need a number proportional to the whole input space, exponential in the input dimension, and deep CNNs stay near chance when every tuple is made equally likely in every class | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md): measured for depth-(L + 1) CNNs and deep fully connected networks on the Random Hierarchy Model with s = 2 and L ≤ 4, with a large-v scaling argument for the correlation threshold and an exact one-step-gradient model of a two-layer network on one patch. | [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) v3 | A finite tree embeds in the hyperbolic plane with worst-case distortion 1 + ε, but because a hyperbolic distance d takes about d bits to write, its coordinates need Θ((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits: logarithmic in the branching, linear in the longest path ℓ, so hyperbolic space is economical for shallow bushy hierarchies and not for deep ones | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). | [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) v4 | Mehta and Schwab's correspondence between Kadanoff's variational renormalization group and restricted Boltzmann machines is an identity of parametrizations, under which an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution; away from that point it does not make training by distribution fitting a renormalization | Mehta and Schwab (2014), [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md), Eqs. 18–22: setting the RG kernel T = −E + H makes the RG coarse Hamiltonian equal the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for every parameter value, and Kadanoff's exactness condition equal to zero KL divergence. | [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) v2 | On sparse hierarchical data, deep networks become insensitive to swapping synonymous parts and to small displacements of informative features at the training-set size at which they learn the task | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. | [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | In next-token prediction on hierarchically generated sequences, the correlation between two tokens falls by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, so a training set of P sequences resolves correlations only out to a distance t*(P) at which they meet sampling noise; learners come to represent the hidden symbols up to that depth, giving loss steps at about v m^(2ℓ−1) examples, and on character-level text the context at which the loss saturates grows as P^(1/(2β)) with β the measured correlation decay | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md) v4 | In variational renormalization over general Boltzmann machines, neither a matched partition function nor Kadanoff's exact trace condition makes a coarse-graining a renormalization: the first holds for joint Hamiltonians whose marginal is not the data, the second for hidden variables that do not interact with the system, so the variables a renormalization keeps must be fixed by a further stated condition | Lin and Tegmark (2016), [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md), arXiv v1–v2 appendix, a part dropped from the journal text: a family of joint Hamiltonians with Z_tot = Z and the wrong marginal, and the remark that any non-interacting pair meets the trace condition. The restricted Boltzmann machine proper needs visible–visible terms for the second construction; that narrows the example, not the claim. Promoted on 2026-10-20 with both constructions re-derived. | [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) v3 | In a two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow, the relative scale of the two layers, which gradient flow conserves, sets the learning regime: balanced layers learn in sigmoidal stages and both build task-specific representations, while strongly unbalanced layers learn exponentially with a static kernel and leave the larger layer task-agnostic | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md) v3 | Mutual information between an input and its representation does not fix the representation's quality: invertible encoders all preserve it exactly, yet under a linear probe some do better than the raw input and some worse | Tschannen, Djolonga, Rubenstein, Gelly & Lucic (2020), [LIT-247](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md), read in [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md). Invertible RealNVP encoders on MNIST halves keep the true MI constant, yet trained with an MI estimator they gain linear-probe accuracy, and one trained adversarially against a linear probe ends "significantly worse than using raw pixels". At matched bound values the encoder architecture decides quality. What makes MI-trained representations good must therefore come from somewhere other than MI. The paper's alternative, that InfoNCE works as metric learning, is argued, not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md) v3 | On a finite augmentation space, at the population optimum of the spectral contrastive loss with k ≥ 2r, linear-probe error is bounded, up to constant and logarithmic factors, by the error of recovering the label from an augmentation divided by the squared sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph | HaoChen, Wei, Gaidon & Ma (2021), [LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md), read in [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md). On a finite augmentation space, with labels recoverable from augmentations up to error α and k ≥ 2r, every population minimizer of the spectral contrastive loss has linear-probe error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where ρ is the sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph (Thm 3.8). The guarantee needs no conditional independence of the views given the label. It is a statement about the population optimum of one loss: it says nothing about what training reaches, nothing about InfoNCE, and its infinite-space extension is asserted, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md) v4 | For a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss on a linear or fixed-kernel model, gradient flow from a small initialization of common scale aligned with the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation learns them one at a time, in order of eigenvalue, and ends at a top spectral solution, which is exactly a minimum-norm zero-loss solution: kernel PCA on K_Γ | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). | [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md) v3 | The Fisher–Rao geometry of a language model's next-token laws over a set of contexts is a function of those laws alone, so models with identical laws share it, while activation geometry changes under invertible reparameterizations of the hidden layer that leave outputs unchanged; in Picozzi's ten transformer, state-space and recurrent models it agreed at a mean rank correlation of 0.88 against 0.62 for activation geometry, and about 9% of the top eigenvector overlap exceeded a null matched to the shared laws | Picozzi (2026), [LIT-936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-936.md), read in [NOTE-755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-755.md), a single-author v1 preprint with code on request. | [THEORY-233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-233.md) v3 | CKA and normalized Bures similarity are the Euclidean and the Bures comparison of normalized kernels, and each bounds the other only within a factor set by the kernels' ranks, so agreement in one does not carry to the other with a dimension-free constant | Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), §5 and App. A.3, read in [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md). Linear kernels only, and the discrepancy is illustrated on Wishart samples, not trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-234.md) v3 | Two softmax next-token predictors induce the same distribution exactly when their embeddings and unembeddings are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces that enter the logits, with arbitrary distortion off them, so a linear relational property is shared by all such models or none when it lies in those subspaces, and can fail to be shared otherwise | Marconato et al. (2024), [LIT-950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-950.md), read in [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md). Exact equality of distributions only, and no experiments. | Active |
| [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md) v3 | A representational similarity index that is invariant to every invertible linear map takes the same value on all representations whose rank equals the number of examples | Kornblith, Norouzi, Lee & Hinton (2019), [LIT-254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-254.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md). If s(X, Z) = s(XA, Z) for every invertible A, and rank(X) = rank(Y) = n, then s(X, Z) = s(Y, Z): any two full-row-rank representations of the same n examples are related by an invertible linear map. The theorem fixes no group; the paper's case for orthogonal invariance plus isotropic scaling is an argument from training dynamics, not a consequence of it. | Active |
| [THEORY-237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-237.md) v3 | The critic-based variational lower bounds on mutual information, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE's and InfoNCE, are relaxations of one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound, and, when the joint and the product of the marginals are mutually absolutely continuous, each attains its supremum over critics only at a critic equal to the log density ratio up to a term its normalization leaves free, where every bound but InfoNCE equals the mutual information | Poole, Ozair, van den Oord, Alemi & Tucker (2019), [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md), read in [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md). Writing q(x\|y) = p(x)e^f/Z(y) in Barber and Agakov's bound gives I_UBA, tight at f = log p(y\|x) + c(y). Jensen gives Donsker–Varadhan, a tangent bound on the log gives TUBA and NWJ (unique optimal critic 1 + log p(x\|y)/p(x)), and NWJ applied to a K-sample problem with the batch mean as normalizer gives InfoNCE. MINE's bias-corrected gradient is the exact gradient of TUBA. A Monte-Carlo DV estimate is neither an upper nor a lower bound. The InfoNCE optimum is cited, not derived, in the source (the record derives it, note of 2026-10-19), and the bias–variance comparisons are on toys. | Active |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v4 | The expected generalization error of an encoder–decoder learner is bounded by the encoder alone, through the KL divergence of its train-and-ghost latents to a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations, for any decoder; and under lossy compression the bound can stay finite for deterministic continuous encoders, whose lossless bound is infinite | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Active |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) v3 | For any joint law of an input and a context, symmetric or not, the top-d left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator attain the minimum, over d-dimensional spans, of worst-case linear-probe approximation error over tasks of compatibility at least 1 − ε, namely (s₁² − (1 − ε)²)/(s₁² − s²_{d+1}) when s_{d+1} < 1 − ε ≤ s₁, though other spans can tie | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. The thesis never works a non-reversible kernel on one space; the note of 2026-10-19 works a three-state one. It says nothing of what a trained network reaches. | Active |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Fitting the same function in the same architecture does not fix the internal decomposition: SGD reproduces three Picbreeder images from random weights without the reuse and factoring of the evolved networks, and perturbing its weights breaks the regularities that perturbing the evolved networks' weights preserves | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) v4 | In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it | Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), Appendix A, and Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), Appendix A.3 and §8, read in [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) and [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Both rotate the same three-unit identity network. The input aligns with h₃ in one basis and with (h₁ + h₂)/√2 in the other, equally well under interchange interventions on the input (re-derived 2026-10-20). The reply says intervening on further variables separates them; that was not checked. Makelov et al. rest their verdict on component boundaries; the reply rests its on the interventions performed. Shown exactly for one constructed network only; whether trained networks have such ties is open (QUESTION-234). | Active |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) v3 | Among ResNet-50s trained on ImageNet with nine objectives and stopped early, seven of which beat softmax cross-entropy's top-1 by up to 0.9 points, fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse by linear probe to datasets whose classes are mostly not ImageNet's (Spearman ρ = −0.93 across the nine; mean accuracy 75.9% for softmax to 48.3% for squared error), and within cosine softmax a higher temperature raises separation and lowers that accuracy; the objectives' representations differ mainly in the last third of the network, and full fine-tuning brings mean transfer to within 1.3 points across them | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. Promoted 2026-10-20 on this one study (ADR-047 v3), narrowed to what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-251.md) | In few-shot classification by a base language model, failures from the choice of examples or from relabelled categories leave the class representations separable and fail at the vocabulary readout | Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md): at five demonstrations, accuracy across draws of examples runs from below 0.1 to about 0.6 while final-layer manifold capacity barely moves, and consistently swapped labels fail while capacity matches gold labels. | [THEORY-269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-269.md) v3 | In OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, how well an affine map from subject to object representation reproduces a factual relation (its LRE causality) tracks how often the relation's subjects and objects co-occur in pretraining, with mean causality above 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, and, across OLMo-7B's eight checkpoints, at whatever step that count is reached | Merullo, Smith, Wiegreffe and Elazar (2025), [LIT-972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-972.md), read in full in [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md). 24 factual relations, three models, eight OLMo-7B checkpoints; r = 0.82 between LRE causality and mean subject–object co-occurrence, above either term's frequency alone. | [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Early in training, image classifiers and language models act on the low-order statistics of their inputs, first-order before second-order, and later lose that sensitivity as they come to use higher-order structure | Belrose et al. | [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) v3 | Perfect concept erasure caps what a representation can keep at the information not about the concept: for X of finite support, if Z is independent of A then I(Z;X) is at most H(X\|A), and a deterministic erasure reaches that cap only when the concept groups' distributions are permutations of one another | Chowdhury et al. | [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md) v3 | A subspace intervention can reproduce the output effect of changing a variable without localizing it, by pairing a direction that varies with the variable but cannot reach the output with one that can reach the output but does not vary on the data | Makelov, Lange and Nanda (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), read in [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). | [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v3 | For a hierarchical multi-index target with isotropic Gaussian inputs and even, separable links, direction k becomes weakly recoverable by the Bayes-optimal estimator at a sample count proportional to its squared weight to the power minus one, so features emerge one at a time through sharp spectral transitions in the number of samples; a target-agnostic spectral estimator attains the thresholds and the optimal weighted error, and a two-layer network whose first layer is that estimator, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). | [THEORY-284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-284.md) v2 | If a feature's values form a compact metric space carried continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere, and cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function of squared feature distance, then every path on the representation manifold is √(−2g′(0)) times as long as the feature path it images, so on-manifold shortest paths recover the feature's intrinsic length metric up to one scale; a homeomorphism alone does not fix it | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy & Whiteley (2025), [LIT-935](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-935.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md). | [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) v4 | For a wide two-layer ReLU network with zero bias on one-dimensional data whose two classes lie on opposite sides of the origin, the tangent kernel is a constant multiple of the initialization kernel, so lazy training leaves the within-class variability of its features, NC1, where initialization put it | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). | [THEORY-299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md) v3 | Structured and translational knowledge-graph embeddings are 0-cochains of a cellular sheaf of vector spaces pulled back from the schema, each triple scored by a norm of the coboundary on its edge and, in the squared-Euclidean form, the whole graph by the sheaf Laplacian; since the zero cochain is always a global section, what they learn is a contrastive margin, not the existence of a section | Gebhart, Hansen and Schrater (2021; AISTATS 2023), [LIT-232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-232.md), §4 and Appendices A and C, read in [NOTE-843](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-843.md). | [THEORY-301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-301.md) v2 | The Procrustes distance between regularization-normalized representations and their average linear-decoding distance bound each other only through the participation ratio of the kernel difference: a small Procrustes distance forces a small decoding distance, but not conversely | Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams (2024), [LIT-257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md), Proposition 3 and App. A.1, read in [NOTE-834](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md). | [THEORY-305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-305.md) v2 | SimCLR's InfoNCE loss, over all n objects with a Gaussian kernel on the unit sphere, equals a graph-Laplacian quadratic form on the augmentation matrix plus the log of InfoNCE's normalizers, which is spectral clustering only in a sense that admits any regularizer and does not make the minimizer the Laplacian's eigenvectors | Tan, Zhang, Yang & Yuan (2023, ICLR 2024), [LIT-227](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-227.md), read in [NOTE-846](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-846.md): Theorem 3.1 and its proof (App. A), Lemma 2.5 and Definition 2.7. | [THEORY-312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-312.md) v2 | The large-batch InfoNCE loss is the negative HSIC between representations and image identity plus a nonnegative log-mean-exp of the centred critic, so it bounds a kernel dependence loss from above | Li, Pogodin, Sutherland & Gretton (2021), [LIT-248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-248.md), eq. 28 and Theorem B.1, read in [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md). | [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) v3 | When two views are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers one view from the other is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor in mean squared error, and it is linear in the contrastive density ratio, so for a bounded label and a square-integrable ratio a linear readout of m random evaluations of the exact ratio approaches it at rate 1/m, with no symmetry between the views required | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. | [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, a novel labelling's linear-probe residual is exactly its part outside the top eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb, so which partition of the unlabelled data is discovered depends on the known classes: ones sharing the target's attribute can remove the residual, and ones sharing a rival attribute can raise it | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). | [THEORY-420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md) | In trained transformers, zeroing a decile of a weight matrix's singular values does damage that falls monotonically with their size in square matrices, whose random-matrix null reaches zero, but not in rectangular ones, whose null has a positive lower edge: there the smallest decile is never the least damaging and can be among the most | Staats, Thamm & Rosenow (2024), [LIT-856](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md), read in [NOTE-659](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-659.md). | [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) v3 | In HGCN embeddings of two synthetic 3-ary trees trained for link prediction or node classification, distance from the origin is only a partial reading of hierarchical level: the root is not innermost (distance 1.8–3.3 against a minimum of 1.2–2.4) and level order is recovered for 69–75% of node pairs; a loss built only on pairwise distances leaves the origin arbitrary | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md). | [THEORY-445](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md) | A network built from group correlations over a discrete split group of plane symmetries, pointwise nonlinearities and coset pooling is equivariant to that group by construction, through the regular representation alone: the group is fixed before training and built into the weight sharing, not found in the data | Cohen & Welling (2016), [LIT-314](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md), read in [NOTE-288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md). | [THEORY-478](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md) v3 | If the diffusion densities' Hellinger distances obey a Hölder bound with exponent θ in d_T / t^(1/β) and are bounded below once d_T exceeds a multiple of t^(1/β), then for 0 < α < θ/β summing scale-weighted hyperbolic distances between diffusion densities over dyadic times gives a distance two-sided equivalent, up to constants, to min{1, d_T^(αβ)} for pairs above the finest scale: it keeps the tree's neighbourhoods and not its global distances; whether a tree's heat kernel, or sampled data, meets the bounds, and with which θ, is not shown | Lin, Coifman, Mishne & Talmon (2023), [LIT-870](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md), read in [NOTE-675](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-675.md). Pairs beyond a radius are only known to be far, which matches the method's best mean average precision and its higher distortion than hyperbolic MDS on five graph benchmarks. A Euclidean distance on the same multiscale features does far worse. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v4 | Under gradient flow averaged over tasks and data, a linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression learns as a two-layer linear network from an aligned start does: when tasks share the input covariance's eigenbasis and the weights start and stay aligned with it, then in the long-context limit each input mode is learned on its own logistic curve whose timescale falls with the square of its variance, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the layer converges to the estimator preconditioned by the inverse input covariance; at finite context length the modes decouple exactly only when inputs are isotropic and the modes start equal, and otherwise couple at order 1/N | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point is ŷ = W Σ̂_x Σ_x⁻¹ x_q as N → ∞. The paper's finite-N form, the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found, holds at finite N only for isotropic inputs with equal modes. The trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Active |
| [THEORY-496](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md) v2 | In few-shot classification and multiple choice by language models up to 175B parameters, whether each demonstration's label is correct contributes little to the gain over zero-shot, while the distribution of the inputs, the label space and the paired format carry most of it | Min et al. Out-of-distribution inputs, random English words as labels, or breaking the input–label pairing each cost far more. | [THEORY-503](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md) | The nearest rank-r matrix to a real matrix in the least-squares norm keeps its r largest singular values and zeroes the rest; it is unique when the r-th and (r+1)-th singular values differ, its squared error is the sum of the dropped squares, and the singular-vector factors that build it are not unique | Eckart & Young (1936), [LIT-330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md), read in full in [NOTE-301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-301.md), which checked the error bound. | [THEORY-504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md) v3 | In the Gemma Scope sparse autoencoders on Gemma 2, the two fidelity measures disagree by site: residual-stream autoencoders cost more next-token loss than MLP or attention ones at comparable fraction of variance unexplained, and base-model autoencoders transfer to the instruction-tuned model by loss more than by variance explained | Lieberum et al. (2024), [LIT-611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md), read in [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md). | [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v3 | From a symmetric, positivity-preserving, positive semi-definite affinity, the normalized Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, so its leading eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data with Euclidean distance equal to diffusion distance, and a density-corrected normalization recovers the Laplace–Beltrami operator independently of how the data were sampled | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), read in full in [NOTE-1441](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1441.md). The finite construction and its isometry are [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md); the paper's own diffusion distance is the one ã^(m) induces, not the inverse-stationary-weighted one. Theorem 2.1 and the α-family are stated without proof; the companion ([LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md)) proves the α-family's limit, Active without boundary as [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md), and its heat-kernel step is [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v3 | In Ganea et al.'s hyperbolic neural networks, linear maps and nonlinearities are Euclidean ones read through the chart at the origin, so a stack of them without biases is a Euclidean network conjugated by that chart, and the curvature acts only through the bias translations and the distance-based output layer | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md) | Measured as mutual 10-nearest-neighbour overlap, competent vision models agree more with one another and better language models agree more with vision models, but the cross-modal score reaches only 0.16 of a possible 1, is the maximum over all layer pairs, and was adopted after a global kernel metric showed only a very weak trend | Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola (2024), [LIT-302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md), read in [NOTE-286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-286.md). It is local neighbourhood agreement that rises with competence, not kernel equality and not convergence to a model of reality. | Active |
| [THEORY-683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md) | Permuting a fixed set of few-shot examples moves a GPT-family model's classification accuracy between near chance and near the supervised state of the art, at every model size tested; the good orders are specific to the model, the spread survives more examples and calibration, and bad orders mostly fail by predicting one label | Lu et al. All 24 orders of four balanced SST-2 examples give accuracies from about 50% to above 85%, in GPT-2 and GPT-3 models of eight sizes; Spearman correlations of order accuracy between sizes lie between −0.35 and 0.27 (175B against 2.7B: 0.05). | [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) v2 | Thresholding linear attribute probes on a language model's embeddings yields a complete concept lattice for any incidence whatever, so the lattice is guaranteed by construction; what the Lattice Representation Hypothesis measured is per-attribute agreement with GPT-4o annotations at F1 70–83, and no lattice law | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). No closure, absorption or recovered-lattice comparison is tested, and the paper's join is not a lattice join as written. | [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) v2 | On a finite augmentation space, over unconstrained functions of the two views, the spectral contrastive and NT-Logistic losses are both minimized at the positive-pair density ratio | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. | [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | For the final embedding and unembedding of a softmax model, the output distribution fixes the representations only up to an invertible linear map, and whether closeness in distribution bounds representational dissimilarity depends on the distance: not for KL in the saturation regime, but yes for the log-likelihood variance distance | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. | [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) v2 | On a finite data set, a symmetric positive affinity normalized to a Markov operator is conjugate to a symmetric one, and its eigenvectors scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals the diffusion distance weighted by the inverse stationary law | Coifman et al. (2005), LIT-981, read in full in NOTE-1441, with the derivation written out here; the 1/π-weighted distance is the companion's (LIT-1246), not the paper's own. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) v2 | For an embedding whose Gram matrix is the absolute co-occurrence deviation matrix at full rank, words on a periodic lattice whose positive and negative co-occurrence parts each depend only on separation have Fourier modes of the lattice as principal components, in degenerate cos/sin pairs with amplitude the square root of the kernel's Fourier transform, and the exponential kernel gives a closed loop with integer frequencies on a periodic lattice and an open curve with non-integer frequencies on an interval | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) v2 | For ReLU networks interpolated linearly between two endpoints, weak additivity and commutativity at every layer make each layer's features exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features, output-layer linearity bounds the path's error by twice the endpoints', and for one hidden layer with interpolating minima linear mode connectivity alone gives the exact case | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), read in [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) with Appendix A's proofs checked: for an L-layer ReLU MLP on a finite dataset, weak additivity of ReLU over the two networks' pre-activations and the commutativity W_A H_B + W_B H_A = W_A H_A + W_B H_B at every layer make the interpolated network's features at every layer exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features (Theorem 1). (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), Lemma 2: for one hidden layer and interpolating minima, linear mode connectivity forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. | [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) v2 | In the hyperbolic plane, a root carrying deg_max ≥ 15 chains of length m, embedded with worst-case distortion 1 + ε for ε ≤ 1, forces some node to hyperbolic distance at least (ℓ/(4ε))·ln(deg_max/(π√2)) from the origin, so fixed-point Poincaré coordinates need Ω((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. | [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | In a spectral contrastive graph that joins labelled known classes to unlabelled data, the least-squares residual of a novel labelling on the top-k eigenspace, with the labelled entries left free, equals exactly the part of the labelling outside that eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) v2 | In the unconstrained-features max-margin problem with k classes under step imbalance and feature dimension at least k − 1, the unique optimal logits are the simplex-encoded labels, every margin equals one, and the classifier and embedding Gram matrices are the two square-root factors of that matrix's singular value decomposition; the geometry is the simplex equiangular tight frame exactly when the classes are balanced or there are two of them | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. | [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) v2 | For the quartic proxy of word2vec with tied weights, symmetric reweighting and constant weights, the rank-d minimisers are the top d eigenvectors of the relative deviation-from-independence matrix M*, scaled by the square roots of their eigenvalues, up to rotation; and from an initialisation aligned with those eigenvectors, gradient flow acquires each one in an independent logistic rise, in order of eigenvalue | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. | [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) v2 | A two-layer linear network trained by gradient flow on white inputs from a decoupled, balanced start learns each singular mode of its input–output correlation in a logistic rise that waits a time of order its inverse strength times the log of the inverse initial scale, so the modes arrive one at a time in order of strength; a single-layer network on the same data learns every mode on one timescale with no plateau, so under these conditions the stages come from the product of layers and the data's spectrum | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. | [THEORY-745](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md) | For the reversible walk p = k/d built from a symmetric non-negative kernel on a finite connected set, the t-step diffusion distance is exactly the Euclidean distance between the coordinates λ_l^t ψ_l, and keeping only the coordinates with \|λ_l\|^t > δ\|λ₁\|^t errs in D_t² by at most δ²\|λ₁\|^{2t}(1/π(x) + 1/π(y)), an absolute bound and not the relative accuracy δ that Coifman and Lafon state; the truncated maps are nested as t grows, so with δ fixed the steps t order a refinement chain by eigenvalue modulus, while untruncated they are all invertible images of one another | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in full in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md). The true bound is absolute and can be large relative to D_t for nearby points. In the refinement sense, the diffusion-map family coarsens with t only through the threshold. Finite sets, counting measure and reversible walks only. It says nothing about the manifold limit or about non-reversible chains. | Active |
| [THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md) | Over a fixed finite set of basis functions, slow feature analysis is a generalized eigenproblem: the outputs that minimize ⟨ẏ²⟩ under zero mean, unit variance and decorrelation are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the derivative covariance against the covariance, in order of slowness, and a stack of such stages, each of whose function spaces contains its inputs, can only keep or lower each of its first m slowness values on the training signal, and may keep them | Wiskott and Sejnowski (2002), [LIT-1249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1249.md), read in full in [NOTE-971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-971.md). Within the span of a fixed basis, the slowest decorrelated unit-variance outputs are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the pencil (⟨ż̃ż̃ᵀ⟩, cov z̃), and each output's slowness is its eigenvalue. A consequence the paper does not draw: a stack of such stages whose function spaces contain their inputs is never faster at a higher stage, componentwise, on the training signal, so in this model "higher is slower" is imposed by the objective, weakly, and can stall. It is about the training signal and a fixed function space. It says nothing about test data, about a generative model, about invariance as opposed to slowness, or about learning dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | A six-layer, 256-unit ReLU network trained by full-batch Adam to regress a sum of sinusoids at 5 to 50 cycles on [0, 1] fits the components in order of frequency, and keeps that order when the amplitudes rise tenfold with frequency, so in this setting the order of acquisition is set by the learner and not by the strength of the target's components | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-775](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md) | With a Gaussian random-walk prior and an instantaneous unit-variance Gaussian encoder, the KL half of the evidence lower bound is the unordered slowness loss plus a constant; with a linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the bound is maximized on the span of the slowest SFA directions whose lag-one autocorrelation exceeds one half, with the basis inside that span unidentified, and on unwhitened input the maximizer is neither SFA's subspace nor invariant to rescaling the input | Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [LIT-1296](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1296.md), read in full in [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md). For linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the maximizer spans the bottom eigenvectors of the difference covariance with eigenvalue μ < 1, each scaled by (μ^{−1/2} − 1)^{1/2} and then rotated arbitrarily. So it recovers SFA's slow span, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, not SFA's features. On raw input it trades variance against slowness. | [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | In networks that learn addition from summed embeddings, the critical training fraction of grokking is the fraction at which the training set's same-answer pairs come to fix the generalising representation up to translation and scale, at every group size, as Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams propose | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Deep networks learn hierarchically generated data from a number of examples set by when the correlations between input patches and the class rise above sampling noise, so detecting those correlations is how they learn the grammar, as Cagnetta and coauthors propose | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training a deep classifier past zero training error generally collapses its last-layer features onto their class means, drives the centred means toward a simplex equiangular tight frame aligned with the classifier, and makes the decision nearest class mean, as Papyan, Han and Donoho propose from their runs | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | The block coarse-graining that maximizes mutual information with the system beyond a buffer picks out the renormalization-group-relevant variables in general, so those variables can be found from samples by information alone, without being known beforehand, as Koch-Janusz and Ringel propose | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Gradient flow on a symmetrized Barlow Twins loss with a linear or fixed-kernel model, from generic small initialization and not only from initialization aligned with the eigenvectors, learns the top eigenvectors of the pairs' symmetrized cross-correlation one at a time in order of eigenvalue and ends at a top spectral solution, as Simon and coauthors derive informally | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | In vision models, compositional generalization to unseen combinations of concepts is driven by the diversity of the combinations seen in training rather than by data volume, and arrives with representations that are linearly factored by concept, as Uselis, Dittadi and Oh propose | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) v2 | Deep classifiers trained with MSE loss stay near the least-squares classifier for their own features and move along the central path by the dynamics of continually renormalized gradient flow, whose equal-rate growth of the whitened class-separation singular values is how they reach neural collapse, as Han, Papyan and Donoho propose | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-798.md) | Independently trained neural encoders of the same data learn latent spaces that differ mainly by an angle-preserving map, a rotation or reflection times a rescaling, so their cosine similarities to shared anchor samples agree across seeds, architectures and languages, as Moschella et al. propose | Moschella, Maiorca, Fumero, Norelli, Locatello & Rodolà (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The hypothesis behind relative representations, filed apart from what their experiments measured ([THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The source assumes it and tests it only through its consequences; it never fits a map between two spaces. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v3 | In trained networks as in constructed ones, interchange interventions on a fixed set of variables can be satisfied equally by alignments related by a change of basis, so which internal direction mediates a high-level variable is fixed only relative to a chosen decomposition into units, and complex models will generally have several distinct, fully correct abstractions | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-805.md) | Volume-maximizing joint-embedding objectives as a class, VICReg and SimCLR as well as MSN and SwAV, carry a prior toward equal-sized clusters, and that prior costs them semantic transfer when the pretraining data are class-imbalanced, including on naturally long-tailed data | The general reading that [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the explicit priors of MSN and SwAV and to one experiment with two to eight classes per batch (batch 033). Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md), argue the prior for the whole class, VICReg through an informal reduction to K-means and SimCLR through a cited equivalence, and read it as the cause of the degradation reported on real long-tailed data. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-808.md) | Transformers trained by next-token prediction on sequence processes whose latent dynamics factor as a tensor product learn to represent the belief state in approximately orthogonal per-factor subspaces of about the factored dimension rather than the joint one, and reach that factored representation first even when noise makes it lossy | The general reading that [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors and the 4-layer GPT-2-style models tested (batch 019). Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md), present next-token training (the paper is titled “Transformers learn factored representations”) as yielding factored, orthogonal belief representations; [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md)'s claims C2 to C4 are each shown on one family of synthetic processes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. It does not include the paper's inference that the preference is architectural (C5), which App. D.4 leaves open, or the claim that the factored form persists at convergence under strong noise, which Fig. 12 contradicts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) v2 | Training a wide network in the lazy, kernel regime does not make its features more collapsed than at initialization, so neural collapse, where it occurs, is something only feature learning produces | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-825](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-825.md) | Hyperbolic graph embedding models trained on task losses that never mention the hierarchy do not place a tree's root nearest the origin, and their distance from the origin orders hierarchical levels only partly | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md), assert for hyperbolic graph models in general what they measured for HGCN on two synthetic trees: the root is not innermost and radius reads level only partly.
